title: Shea butter body lotion
subtitle: A light whipped lotion for daily body moisturising
excerpt: A water-in-oil lotion made with shea butter, almond oil, and emulsifying wax, scented with lavender essential oil. Spreads easily and absorbs quickly. An emulsified lotion like this requires a broad-spectrum preservative because it contains a water phase. Gives about 200 g of lotion. Shelf life 3 months.
sourceNotes: Emulsified body lotion formulation: oil phase (shea butter + sweet almond oil) + water phase (distilled water) + emulsifier (BTMS-50 or Emulsifying Wax NF). Both phases heated to 70-75°C, then combined with thorough mixing to form a stable emulsion. Preservative (Optiphen or Leucidal Liquid): required for all water-containing cosmetic formulations; water activity supports bacterial and fungal growth without a preservative. Optiphen (phenoxyethanol + caprylyl glycol) at 1% is effective across pH 4-8 and suits this lotion. Lavender EO: added below 40°C to avoid evaporation; safe at 1-2% in a leave-on body lotion under IFRA guidelines. Batch: 200 g is a practical minimum for making a stable emulsion.

recipe.batchNotes: A 400 g batch is more efficient if making for the whole household. Emulsions become easier to form reliably once you've made 2-3 batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Lotion is ready to use once cooled and set. A hand whisk is sufficient for this batch size; a stick blender makes the emulsion more stable in a larger batch.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 3 months with a broad-spectrum preservative. Without preservative: use within 1 week (keep refrigerated). Discard at any sign of separation, off smell, or discolouration.

glossaryTerms.definition: A blend of waxes and surfactants that allows oil and water to combine into a stable cream or lotion. Without an emulsifier, oil and water separate immediately. Common options: Emulsifying Wax NF, BTMS-50.

A cosmetic preservative effective against both bacteria and fungi. Required in any product containing a water phase. Optiphen (phenoxyethanol + caprylyl glycol) is a common choice for home formulations.

content.text: Heat the oil phase (shea, almond oil, emulsifying wax) in a heatproof bowl over simmering water until fully melted and liquid, about 70°C.
In a separate jug, heat the distilled water to 70-75°C.
Pour the water into the oil phase in a slow, steady stream while whisking continuously. Whisk for 3-5 minutes until the mixture turns white and creamy.
Continue whisking as it cools. Once below 40°C, stir in the preservative and lavender essential oil.
Pour into the pump bottle once fully cooled and thickened.
3 months with a broad-spectrum preservative. Store in a cool place away from direct sunlight. Discard immediately if the lotion separates, smells off, or changes colour.
